events.title: Pyu People Enter Myanmar
events.description: The Pyu people migrated from southwestern China into central Myanmar's Irrawaddy River valley, establishing early civilization. Pyu city-states were influenced by Indian culture, practicing Buddhism and Hinduism.

events.title: Bamar People Enter Myanmar
events.description: The Bamar people migrated from present-day Yunnan into Myanmar, settling in the middle Irrawaddy River region. The Bamar gradually became Myanmar's dominant ethnic group.

events.title: Pagan Kingdom Founded
events.description: The Bamar people established the Pagan Kingdom, Myanmar's first unified kingdom. Pagan became Myanmar's political and religious center.

events.title: Reign of Anawrahta
events.description: King Anawrahta conquered the Mon people and unified central and southern Myanmar. He promoted Theravada Buddhism, making it Myanmar's state religion. The Pagan Kingdom entered its golden age.

events.title: Pagan Pagoda Construction
events.description: Pagan built thousands of pagodas and temples, including masterpieces like the Shwezigon Pagoda and Ananda Temple. Pagan became Southeast Asia's Buddhist cultural center, with its pagoda-studded landscape still visible today.

events.title: Mongol Invasion and Pagan's Decline
events.description: Kublai Khan sent Mongol forces to invade Myanmar, defeating the Pagan Kingdom which then declined. Myanmar fragmented into multiple small states.

events.title: Shan Rule Period
events.description: After Pagan's fall, Shan people established the Ava Kingdom, controlling central and northern Myanmar. Meanwhile, Mon people established the Hanthawaddy Kingdom in the south. Myanmar was divided.

events.title: Toungoo Dynasty Founded
events.description: Bamar leader Tabinshwehti established the Toungoo Dynasty, beginning Myanmar's reunification. The Toungoo Dynasty became Myanmar's second unified dynasty.

events.title: Bayinnaung's Conquests
events.description: King Bayinnaung conquered Shan states, Arakan, and Mon territories, unifying Myanmar. The Toungoo Dynasty reached its peak, becoming a Southeast Asian power.

events.title: Conquest of Siam (Thailand)
events.description: Burmese forces captured Ayutthaya (Thai capital), making Siam a Burmese vassal. Burmese-Siamese conflicts continued for centuries.

events.title: Konbaung Dynasty Founded
events.description: Alaungpaya overthrew the Toungoo Dynasty and established the Konbaung Dynasty (Myanmar's last dynasty).

events.title: Alaungpaya Unifies Myanmar
events.description: Alaungpaya reunified Myanmar, conquering Mon and Shan territories. The Konbaung Dynasty entered its golden age.

events.title: First Anglo-Burmese War
events.description: Britain and Myanmar went to war, with Myanmar defeated. The Treaty of Yandabo ceded Arakan and Tanintharyi to Britain, with £1 million in reparations.

events.title: Second Anglo-Burmese War
events.description: Britain attacked Myanmar again, occupying Pegu and Yangon. Myanmar lost Lower Burma, with Britain controlling southern coastal areas.

events.title: Third Anglo-Burmese War
events.description: British forces captured Mandalay and captured the last king, Thibaw. The Konbaung Dynasty fell, and Myanmar became a complete British colony.

events.title: Myanmar Annexed to British India
events.description: Britain annexed Myanmar to British India, administering it as a province. British rule changed Myanmar's social structure, introducing Indian laborers and merchants.

events.title: Rise of Burmese Nationalism
events.description: Student movements emerged at Yangon University, demanding autonomy and independence. Burmese nationalism began developing.

events.title: Myanmar Separated from British India
events.description: Myanmar became a directly ruled British colony, no longer part of British India. First Premier Ba Maw led a semi-autonomous government.

events.title: Japanese Occupation
events.description: During the Pacific War, Japanese forces occupied Myanmar, expelling British forces. Aung San and other Burmese nationalists initially cooperated with Japan, forming the Burma Defence Army.

events.title: Japan Establishes Puppet 'Independence'
events.description: Japan supported Ba Maw in establishing a nominally independent Burmese government, but it was actually a puppet regime.

events.title: Aung San's Anti-Japanese Uprising
events.description: Aung San led the Burma Defence Army in uprising, turning to support Allies against Japan. After Japan's defeat, Britain reoccupied Myanmar.

events.title: Panglong Agreement
events.description: Aung San signed the Panglong Agreement with Shan, Kachin, and Chin ethnic minority representatives, agreeing to establish a unified Union of Burma. This was the foundation for Myanmar's independence.

events.title: Assassination of Aung San
events.description: Myanmar's independence leader General Aung San and six cabinet members were assassinated during a meeting by political rivals. Aung San is revered as 'Father of the Nation,' but did not live to see Myanmar's independence.

events.title: Myanmar Independence
events.description: Myanmar officially gained independence from British rule, establishing the Union of Burma. U Nu became first Prime Minister. January 4 became Myanmar's Independence Day.

events.title: Civil War and Division
events.description: After independence, Myanmar plunged into civil war with communist rebellions and ethnic minorities demanding autonomy. Armed organizations like Karen and Shan fought government forces, with conflicts continuing today.

events.title: Military Coup
events.description: General Ne Win launched a military coup, overthrowing the U Nu government and establishing military rule. Myanmar began a half-century of military dictatorship.

events.title: 'Burmese Way to Socialism'
events.description: Ne Win implemented the 'Burmese Way to Socialism,' nationalizing private enterprises and pursuing isolationist policies. The economy declined, with Myanmar falling from Southeast Asia's wealthiest to poorest nations.

events.title: New Constitution and Socialist Republic
events.description: A new constitution was promulgated, changing the country name to 'Socialist Republic of the Union of Burma.' Ne Win continued holding real power.

events.title: 8888 Democracy Movement
events.description: Citizens launched massive pro-democracy protests (called 8888 because it occurred on August 8). The military opened fire, killing thousands. Ne Win was forced to step down.

events.title: Military Junta Takes Control
events.description: General Saw Maung launched a coup, establishing the State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC). Military rule continued.

events.title: Country Renamed Myanmar
events.description: The military government changed the English name from 'Burma' to 'Myanmar' and Rangoon to 'Yangon.' However, many countries and democrats continue using Burma.

events.title: Election and Military Refuses Power Transfer
events.description: The military held elections, with Aung San Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy winning overwhelming victory. But the military refused to transfer power, declaring election results invalid.

events.title: Aung San Suu Kyi Under House Arrest
events.description: Aung San Suu Kyi (daughter of General Aung San) was placed under house arrest for 15 years by the military government for leading the democracy movement. She received the Nobel Peace Prize, becoming a symbol of Myanmar's democracy.

events.title: Capital Moved to Naypyidaw
events.description: The military government suddenly moved the capital from Yangon to the inland new city Naypyidaw. Reasons for the move are unclear, possibly for military security.

events.title: Saffron Revolution
events.description: Monks led anti-government demonstrations (named for their saffron-colored robes). The military brutally suppressed them, attacking monasteries and arresting monks.

events.title: Cyclone Nargis Disaster
events.description: Powerful Cyclone Nargis struck Myanmar, causing about 140,000 deaths, Myanmar's worst natural disaster. The military government's poor response and refusal of international aid drew international criticism.

events.title: New Constitution Referendum
events.description: The military promoted a new constitution referendum, paving the way for 'transition' to civilian government. But the constitution reserved enormous military power, mandating 25% of parliamentary seats for military appointees.

events.title: Election and Suu Kyi Released
events.description: Myanmar held its first election in 20 years, with military-backed Union Solidarity and Development Party winning. Aung San Suu Kyi was released after the election.

events.title: Civilian Government Formed
events.description: Thein Sein became president, the military junta dissolved, and a nominally civilian government formed. Thein Sein implemented political and economic reforms, with Myanmar beginning 'democratization.'

events.title: Aung San Suu Kyi Enters Parliament
events.description: In by-elections, Aung San Suu Kyi was elected to parliament, with NLD winning 43 seats. Aung San Suu Kyi ended years of political isolation.

events.title: Rakhine State Violence
events.description: Violent clashes erupted in western Rakhine State between Buddhists and Rohingya Muslims, with hundreds killed and tens of thousands displaced. The Rohingya issue began gaining international attention.

events.title: NLD Wins Election
events.description: The National League for Democracy won a landslide victory in elections, gaining an absolute majority in parliament. This was a historic democratic victory for Myanmar.

events.title: Aung San Suu Kyi Leads Government
events.description: Due to constitutional restrictions (her husband was foreign), Aung San Suu Kyi couldn't become president but served as State Counsellor (de facto leader). Her civilian government took power.

events.title: Rohingya Crisis
events.description: Large-scale violence erupted in Rakhine State, with Myanmar's military conducting 'clearance operations' against the Rohingya, causing about 700,000 Rohingya to flee to Bangladesh. The UN called it 'ethnic cleansing,' and Aung San Suu Kyi faced international criticism for not condemning the military.

events.title: NLD Wins Again
events.description: The National League for Democracy won elections again. But the military alleged electoral fraud, refusing to accept results.

events.title: Military Coup
events.description: Myanmar's military launched a coup, detaining Aung San Suu Kyi and government officials and seizing power. The military declared a state of emergency, interrupting Myanmar's democratization process.

events.title: Civil Disobedience Movement
events.description: Citizens launched massive anti-coup demonstrations and civil disobedience movement (CDM). The military violently suppressed protests, causing thousands of deaths.

events.title: Crackdown Escalates
events.description: The military used live ammunition against protesters, causing over 100 deaths in a single day. International community condemned military atrocities, but sanctions had limited effect.

events.title: National Unity Government Formed
events.description: Opposition MPs formed the 'National Unity Government' (NUG) to oppose the military junta. NUG formed People's Defense Forces (PDF), beginning armed resistance.

events.title: Ongoing Civil War
events.description: Myanmar plunged into civil war, with People's Defense Forces and ethnic armed organizations uniting against the military junta. Conflict has caused massive civilian casualties and refugees, with Myanmar's economy collapsing.

events.title: Resistance Forces Make Progress
events.description: Ethnic armed groups and People's Defense Forces launched offensives in multiple areas, capturing numerous towns and military positions. Military junta control weakened, though it still controls major cities.

events.title: Continued Turmoil
events.description: Myanmar's conflict continues, with humanitarian crisis worsening. Millions displaced, economy collapsed, military junta and resistance forces deadlocked. International community calls for peaceful resolution, but prospects remain unclear.
